web.title: Heavy Cream vs. Half-and-Half vs. Coffee Creamer - Healthline
web.description:
# Heavy Cream vs. Half-and-Half vs. Coffee Creamer: What's the Difference?
## They’re different but have similar uses
### Heavy cream
In the US, the FDA defines heavy cream as having no less than 36% milkfat ( [1](https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/scripts/cdrh/cfdocs/cfcfr/CFRSearch.cfm?fr=131.150)).

### Half-and-half
The FDA requires half-and-half to contain between 10.5% to 18% milkfat ( [2](https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/scripts/cdrh/cfdocs/cfcfr/CFRSearch.cfm?fr=131.180)).

Fat-free varieties of half-and-half are also widely available and typically made by combining skim milk with corn syrup instead of cream, resulting in a fat-free product that’s higher in added sugar.
